## What's new

Threadnote 4 beta.32 carries the large-repository graph work through materialization, querying, visualization, migration, and release evidence.

- Persisted dirty overlays now preserve workspace-scoped TypeScript lookup tiers through package barrels. Calls, inheritance, and their persisted analysis summaries remain structurally identical to a full rebuild, including in multi-package workspaces with same-name scope candidates.
- Code-graph builds now materialize directly into persistent, query-invisible building snapshots instead of multi-gigabyte connection-private temporary B-trees. Deterministic checkpoints make interrupted cold builds resumable, while leases and garbage collection keep abandoned work bounded without exposing partial snapshots.
- Large graph writes use compact reference-candidate and lexical representations, bounded pages, sorted bulk inserts, and explicit writer telemetry. The release retains production-shaped 100k lexical evidence and rejects graph schema generations newer than the installed runtime.
- Parser workers are started lazily, share bounded host capacity, and keep their retained memory under reviewed limits. Concurrent readers, indexers, worktrees, and agents remain isolated while sharing safe committed facts.
- Exact-head development installs build and activate a standalone payload from the current clean commit, terminate superseded managed processes when requested, and record verifiable source provenance. Process diagnostics also surface old standalone versions instead of incorrectly reporting no live Threadnote work.
- Manager graph catalogs, overview and detail queries, scope summaries, lazy node expansion, and WebGL rendering are snapshot-pinned, paged, and bounded. The Manager now has a dedicated graph-query flow in addition to node filtering, with stale responses rejected when users switch repository, scope, snapshot, or query.
- Manager startup no longer waits for a large catalog before rendering. Camera state remains stable during refresh and expansion, maximum-cardinality focus layouts use bounded collision work, and storage/progress views account for active building snapshots.
- Migration and post-update eligibility are now based on recoverable source state, not version alone. Fresh installs and already-migrated homes are not prompted, older beta receipts are normalized safely, concurrent canonical writes are preserved, and resumed migrations verify exact target content before completion.
- Shared auto-sync defers cleanly under healthy lock contention and forces the next successful refresh to reindex, avoiding stale recall without breaking another agent's active operation.
- The Performance site and external-repository harness fail closed unless the retained artifact proves exact source provenance, polyglot and Bazel controls, incremental/full parity, concurrent-worktree isolation, concise MCP output, bounded Manager queries, real process telemetry, and privacy-safe public metadata. Whole-graph summary checks now stay on the exact persisted aggregate path instead of accidentally requesting bounded topology analysis.
- Repair dry-run output now prints a valid continuation command, and packaged release checks verify the current Threadnote logo and website identity.

Existing beta installations can update in place:

```bash
threadnote update --beta
```

Fresh beta installation:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kashkovsky/threadnote/v4.0.0-beta.32/scripts/install.sh |
  sh -s -- --beta
```
